evals.prompt: Add declarative Pi settings to my public dotfiles, but let my private work-dotfiles repo add a company package and let one laptop disable it locally. Pi only reads one settings.json and keeps auth and sessions beside it.
evals.expected_output: Uses the four standard layers, avoids linking the mutable Pi directory, defines deterministic merge and disable behavior, preserves unmanaged state, and excludes credentials.

evals.prompt: Two repos need to contribute SSH configuration. Right now the second repo replaces the first repo's ~/.ssh/config.d symlink. Redesign this so both can coexist and machine-only aliases stay untracked.
evals.expected_output: Assigns file-level ownership, uses tracked and local fragment tiers with lexical ordering, and avoids whole-directory ownership conflicts.

evals.prompt: Review this config loader: it recursively merges dictionaries and concatenates every list, catches JSON errors and prints a warning, then rewrites the app's complete state directory on each bootstrap run.
evals.expected_output: Flags array concatenation, swallowed errors, mutable-directory replacement, unclear ownership, stale-entry handling, and missing idempotency/preservation tests.
